title: Peer/typing federation calls generated for remote users who have opted out
description: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md line 904 specifies that for federated chats, the server SHOULD invoke Peer/typing on each remote participant's home server. A remote participant's receiveTypingIndicators preference lives on their own mailbox, which the originating server cannot read. The originating server therefore always makes the Peer/typing federation call, and the remote server checks the preference and silently drops it. In a direct chat where the remote user has receiveTypingIndicators: false, every typing event (up to 1 per 3 seconds) generates a cross-server federation call that accomplishes nothing. There is no mechanism for a remote server to advertise opt-out preference to the originating server, and no provision for the originating server to suppress outbound Peer/typing calls based on known-cached preference. The federation spec (JMAP-CHAT-FED) should consider whether a remote preference advertisement mechanism is warranted, or at minimum document that this waste is accepted as a privacy tradeoff.
close_reason: Fixed in review fix wave or recorded as accepted design decision.
